A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SELF-REDTEAM research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable matching despite extensive reformatting and added material.

before.justification: v3 reports original Qwen and Llama fine-tuning experiments, safety and capability evaluations, training curves, ablations, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds dynamic-attack evaluations, a reward-judge comparison, attack-strategy classification, and attacker-refusal measurements.

M1.justification: The shared-policy self-play procedure, hidden CoT, reward components, role-specific Re++ normalization, and auxiliary self-distilled SFT remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and Appendix A retain the same procedure; expanded loss notation and testing another reward judge do not establish an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: v4 adds live, target-adaptive single-turn PAIR and AutoDAN evaluation scenarios alongside retained static benchmarks and multi-turn X-Teaming. v3 already included precomputed PAIR/AutoDAN attacks within HarmBench, but these were transferred attack inputs rather than the newly reported adaptive evaluations. Training datasets and other task coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The existing baseline and ablation methods remain, including Attacker-Only, Defender-Only, CoT/SFT variants, LLM-LAT, and CircuitBreaker. The latter comparisons already appeared in v3 Appendix D.2. PAIR/AutoDAN supply new evaluation threats against the retained base-versus-fine-tuned comparison, while Qwen3Guard varies the training judge.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include Qwen3Guard training with WildGuard-scored evaluation, live PAIR/AutoDAN evaluated using HarmBench-Llama-2-13B, GPT-4o classification of approximately 250 attacks into 35 tactics, and refusal classification over 3,000–5,000 attacks per model from three checkpoints. Reported X-Teaming configurations now omit Llama. Existing training budgets, static evaluation settings, and retained X-Teaming procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds reward-judge sensitivity testing (Table 3), strategy-level diversity analysis with benign-seed and RL-only checks (Appendix D.5), and a systematic cross-model investigation of attacker refusals (Appendix E.2). These substantially extend the robustness and mechanism diagnostics. Existing CoT/SFT ablations, perplexity analysis, computational comparisons, and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: v3's Reproducibility Statement says Table 1 and ablation results average at least three independent trials; v4 removes this general disclosure. Three-run training curves with 95% confidence intervals and eight-checkpoint bootstrap plots remain, while new Table 3 explicitly reports three-run averages. The PDFs do not establish increased repetition or new uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Existing main, ablation, and safeguarding table values are retained apart from rounding. v4 adds dynamic-attack scores, Qwen3Guard-trained results, strategy entropy of 2.20 versus 0.90, and attacker-refusal rates across five models. For example, newly reported Qwen2.5-14B PAIR ASRs are 0.218 for the base model and 0.108 after SELF-REDTEAM. The Llama X-Teaming pair, 76% versus 42%, disappears. Section 6 also incorrectly attributes the retained perplexity value 8.62 to Attacker-Only, although both appendix tables identify the base model.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and its original contradiction proof remain, but new Appendix B.1 introduces constrained attacker/defender policy sets, a constrained zero-sum game, and regularized objectives. It additionally asserts equilibrium recovery with increasing penalties and bounded finite-penalty approximation error. This substantially extends the theoretical connection claimed between the idealized game and implemented training, without providing a corresponding new proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction expand advertised robustness coverage from 12 to 14 safety evaluations and explicitly position SELF-REDTEAM as a drop-in alternative to standard alignment. The central self-play, hidden-CoT, conditional equilibrium-safety, 17.8% diversity, and up-to-95% safety-improvement claims remain.

C2.justification: v4 adds arguments against judge-specific reward hacking, interprets tactic classification as evidence of strategy-level novelty, and expands the rationale for single-model self-improvement. Appendix E reframes attacker refusal from an emergent safeguard into Llama-specific inherited alignment that purportedly leaves defender improvement intact. The earlier explicit limitations concerning single-turn training and specialized reasoning/domain evaluation are removed. Appendix B.1 also newly distinguishes equilibrium safety from convergence guarantees.

D1.justification: v4 discloses t-SNE/DBSCAN parameters, the strategy-classification procedure, the Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking refusal judge, and use of HarmBench implementations for PAIR/AutoDAN. Conversely, it removes the OpenRLHF implementation disclosure and the exact all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedding-model identifier. Core training hyperparameters, hardware details, and the code hyperlink remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds positioning relative to AdvGame, WaltzRL, SPIRAL, and population-based adversarial RL, alongside references supporting the added attacks, Qwen3Guard, and penalty-method discussion. It removes the introductory news citations and formal LlamaGuard reference. Numerous other bibliography changes update or consolidate already-cited works rather than introduce different research.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and results narrative are extensively rewritten and condensed. The quotation/news opening is removed, method and experiment subsections are reorganized, ablations receive a separate subsection, and Ethics becomes Impact Statement. The Reproducibility Statement and appendix contents page disappear, while Appendix E is reorganized into Additional Discussion.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text and references, substantially resizing and repositioning displays. It adds a zero-sum-game schematic and tables for judge comparison, metric notation, strategy diversity, and refusal rates. The appendix X-Teaming table moves into the main text and gains attack-method columns; existing plots are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added adaptive attacks, alternative training judge, and strategy/refusal diagnostics provide a limited net improvement by directly testing robustness and diversity questions less thoroughly examined in v3. This benefit is tempered by lost trial-count, implementation, and limitations disclosures and the misidentified perplexity baseline in Section 6. Appendix B.1 also does not establish that its constrained game admits the safe fallback required by the retained proof. The empirical validation improves, while the new theoretical bridge remains inadequately justified.
